concepts.def: Three-dimensional artwork created by carving, casting, modelling or constructing.
Subtractive process removing material from stone, wood or other solid (e.g., Michelangelo's David).
Pouring liquid material (bronze, plaster) into a mould to make multiple copies.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Sculpture and Three-Dimensional Studies — a core area of GCSE Art & Design.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Sculpture and Three-Dimensional Studies brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Sculpture and Three-Dimensional Studies.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
